value.rationale: Two-vertex loss is the first natural nontrivial erasure pattern beyond the one-vertex transitivity class; the edge/nonedge split completely classifies the 136 punctures of a canonical seventeen-point Ramsey and conference graph. It detects a two-class difference in surviving integral second homology and gives actual primitive inclusion ranks, furnishing a concrete local topological resilience profile. The exact pair-orbit result is not merely the ambient Euler count; simple connectivity of both induced restrictions is established by separately exhaustive Morse matchings. No broader conjecture is needed for this finite natural classification to have mathematical value.
